title: Measuring the Premium Arrears on a ShieldCare Plan
content:
## The measure

The arrears standing on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan is measured from the plan's own
premium history and from the outstanding premium figure carried on the plan record. Read together:
the premium entries booked on the plan, being the premium billed on it less the premium received
against it; the outstanding premium recorded on the plan; and the standing of the plan itself.

| What the records show | How the arrears is measured |
| --- | --- |
| the premium entries booked on the plan add up to more than the outstanding premium recorded on it, and the plan stands active | the arrears is rebuilt from the premium entries booked on the plan, as the premium instalments billed less the premium payments received |
| the plan stands active, and those entries add up to no more than the outstanding premium recorded on it | the arrears is the periods whose grace has fully run, priced at the plan's monthly premium |
| every other plan | the arrears is the outstanding premium recorded on the plan |

**The periods whose grace has fully run** are the unpaid periods less the most recent period billed
where that period is still inside the plan's grace days, and never fewer than none. A period is
still inside the plan's grace days while fewer days have passed since its first day than the plan's
grace days allow.

### Both sides of the comparison

Where the netted premium entries come to exactly the outstanding premium recorded on the plan, they
do not come to more than it, so the second row governs on a plan standing active. Only entries
netting above the recorded figure reach the first row. A plan that does not stand active reaches
neither of the first two rows, whatever its entries show.

### A case on hypothetical figures

A plan that does not stand active takes its arrears from the outstanding premium recorded on it, whatever its
entries show. Take instead a plan standing active that carries an outstanding premium of 24.00. Where its
history shows premium billed of 40.00 and premium received of 20.00, the entries net to 20.00, which is not
more than 24.00, and the arrears is the periods whose grace has fully run priced at the plan's monthly premium.
Where its history shows premium billed of 60.00 and premium received of 24.00, the entries net to 36.00, which
is more than 24.00, and the arrears is rebuilt as the instalments billed less the payments received.
